title: Implement check-in service (CheckInVisitor)

title: Implement consumption allocation engine

Builds timeline from MeterReadingEvents, analyzes each period (present visitors, manual entries), allocates consumption, distributes empty-house pool. Returns per-visitor breakdown. Thorough specs for algorithm correctness, overlapping stays (E1), empty periods (E2), manual entries (E4, E5).

title: Investigate production CrashLoopBackOff
description:
Site at sepot.kopernici.cz returning 503. Pod in CrashLoopBackOff with 17+ restarts.

## Known facts
- v0.0.4 was the last successfully built Docker image (lint started failing at v0.0.5)
- v0.0.7 image just built successfully but Flux hasn't picked it up yet (or pod still stuck)
- Docker job was skipped for v0.0.5 and v0.0.6 due to lint failure
- The site was working on v0.0.4 after the Tailwind fix

## Hypotheses

1. **Flux picked up v0.0.7 but pod startup is failing** — the new code (Czech i18n) might have a runtime error (missing translation key, bad YAML syntax, etc.) that crashes Rails on boot

2. **SQLite DB issue on PVC** — a failed migration or corrupt DB from a previous attempt could cause the entrypoint (db:prepare + app:setup) to crash

3. **Infrastructure/node issue** — the K3s node may have restarted or the PVC became unavailable, causing repeated crash loops unrelated to our code

4. **Flux hasn't reconciled yet** — still running v0.0.4 which was working, but something else caused it to start crashing (OOM, resource limits, etc.)

5. **Entrypoint race condition** — bin/docker-entrypoint runs db:prepare and app:setup on every start; if the PVC mount is slow or unavailable, SQLite operations fail

## Next step
Run kubectl logs on the pod to identify the actual crash reason.
